# Typed flag schema introspection
**Issue:** #2326
**Date:** 2026-09-29
**Verified at:** 84d0da5
**Confidence:** 0.90
**Status:** SPEC

## Executive Summary
Flag consumers have no optional schema-specific type interface. Add `SchemaTyper` and `SchemaItemsTyper` without changing `Flag` or the existing help-text `TypeName` contract. Built-in flags, inverse booleans, and adapted standard-library flags expose the accepted value's schema category. [VERIFIED: `flag.go` › `Flag`, `DocGenerationFlag`; `flag_impl.go` › `TypeName`; `flag_ext.go` › `Get`]

## Current State / Root Cause
`TypeName` collapses numeric widths into CLI names and reports slice element names rather than an array category. The public `Flag` contract has no JSON Schema introspection methods. `extFlag.Get()` returns its wrapped `flag.Getter` value. [VERIFIED: `flag_impl.go` › `TypeName`; `flag.go` › `Flag`; `flag_ext.go` › `Get`]

## What Already Works
Concrete built-ins are `FlagBase` aliases, including boolean, signed/unsigned integer, floating point, string, slices, map, duration and timestamp. The inverse boolean is separate. [VERIFIED: `rg -n '^type .*Flag =|FlagBase\[' flag_*.go` on 2026-09-29; `flag_bool_with_inverse.go` › `BoolWithInverseFlag`]

## Contract (Verified)
| Field / Behavior | Type | Evidence | Tag |
|---|---|---|---|
| Existing parsing interface | `Flag` | `flag.go` › `Flag` | VERIFIED |
| Existing help type | `TypeName() string` | `flag.go` › `DocGenerationFlag`; `flag_impl.go` › `TypeName` | VERIFIED |
| New optional schema category | `SchemaTyper.SchemaType() string` | issue #2326 in task brief | VERIFIED requirement |
| New optional array element category | `SchemaItemsTyper.SchemaItemsType() string` | issue #2326 in task brief | VERIFIED requirement |
| Adapted standard flags expose value through getter | `any` | `flag_ext.go` › `Get` | VERIFIED |

## Clients
| Client | Live? | Evidence |

| Existing in-repo help/documentation consumers | yes | `rg -n 'TypeName\(' -g '*.go'` on 2026-09-29; unaffected existing method |
| Future schema generator and external library clients | unknown | Issue #2326 requests optional interfaces; external source unavailable in assigned isolated arm [ASSUMED, 2026-09-29] |

## Deploy Order
Library implementation and godoc snapshots ship together. New external consumers can type-assert either optional interface after taking this library version; existing consumers continue using `Flag`/`TypeName`. [ASSUMED from additive method design, 2026-09-29]

## Implementation Options
Picked: one shared value-to-schema helper called by `FlagBase` and `extFlag`, with inverse boolean methods returning constants. This keeps mappings consistent and lets `extFlag` inspect `e.Get()` exactly as requested. [ASSUMED design]
Alternative: separate type switches in each implementation duplicate mappings and risk divergence; no independent benefit found.
Real usage: `extFlag` is constructed from standard flags in `command_setup.go` and existing tests; built-ins are aliases instantiated directly in flag files/tests. `TypeName` is used by documentation/help and remains separate. [VERIFIED: `command_setup.go` › `extFlag`; `flag_test.go` › `TestExtFlag`; `rg -n 'TypeName\(' -g '*.go'` on 2026-09-29]

## Changes

MODIFIED: `godoc-current.txt` — regenerate public documentation from source.

Callers: `Flag`/`DocGenerationFlag` — `rg -n 'Flag\b|DocGenerationFlag|TypeName\(' -g '*.go'` finds parsing/help consumers (same: interfaces unchanged); new `SchemaTyper`/`SchemaItemsTyper` have no existing callers (changes: new tests and future consumers). `FlagBase` constructors are alias literals in `flag_*` tests (same parsing behavior). `extFlag` construction is in `command_setup.go`, `flag_test.go`, `flag_int_test.go`, `flag_uint_test.go` (changes: optional type assertions). `BoolWithInverseFlag` literals are in tests/examples (changes: optional type assertions). [VERIFIED: cited `rg` commands on 2026-09-29]
Downstream: generated godoc snapshots are compared with exported API documentation (`scripts/build.go` › `GenerateActionFunc`, `V3Diff`); CLI parsing consumes `Flag` methods and should see no changed behavior. [VERIFIED: `scripts/build.go`; `flag.go` › `Flag`]
History: `git log --oneline -i --grep=fix -- flag.go flag_impl.go flag_bool_with_inverse.go flag_ext.go` includes inverse-bool help and extFlag default fixes; test unparsed zero-value inverse bool and pre/post-parse wrapped standard values. [VERIFIED: command on 2026-09-29]

## User Flow Impact
| Flow | Change |
|---|---|
| Schema generator type-asserts a flag | New category and optional item category |
| CLI parses built-in or adapted flag | Existing parsing behavior preserved |
| Help text uses `TypeName` | Existing label behavior preserved |

## Change Dependency Matrix
| Applied alone | Result |
|---|---|
| Interfaces without methods | Consumers can type-assert but built-ins report nothing |
| Methods without common mapping | Category logic may diverge between built-ins and adapted flags |
| Source without godoc snapshots | Public API baseline is stale |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-1: Every built-in scalar family reports its category: boolean, integer, number, string, duration, or date-time; single-value flags report no item category.
  Tricky inputs: zero-value `DurationFlag`, zero-value `TimestampFlag`, signed/unsigned width aliases, zero-value `BoolWithInverseFlag`.
- [ ] AC-2: Every built-in slice reports `array` plus the correct element category; string map reports `object` and no item category.
  Tricky inputs: nil `StringSliceFlag`, nil `Uint64SliceFlag`, nil `StringMapFlag`, empty slice value.
- [ ] AC-3: An `extFlag` reports categories from `e.Get()` for all standard getter scalar branches and cleanly mapped custom collection getters; unknown or non-getter values report empty categories.
  Tricky inputs: zero-value standard duration, false standard bool, nil slice getter, empty slice getter, opaque struct getter, non-getter `flag.Value`.
- [ ] AC-4: The two interfaces remain optional, existing help type labels stay the same, and both godoc snapshots match regenerated current documentation.
  Tricky inputs: custom `Flag` implementation without new methods, inverse bool `TypeName`, generic custom value without a clean schema mapping.

## Success Metrics

## Out of Scope
Full JSON Schema document generation and changes to CLI parsing/help formatting. Third-party custom flags may implement either optional interface themselves.

## Decision Points
No missing product decision: the requested type vocabulary and empty fallback are explicit. The exact treatment of `GenericFlag` depends on its custom value and will be blank when no clean mapping exists. [ASSUMED, 2026-09-29]
